label: Expedition sequence
quiz: Which sequence correctly describes Legazpi's expedition?

retry: Why should departure and settlement appear separately on a timeline?
They are different events that happened at different stages
A departure date proves every later outcome
Every event belongs on the arrival date
Separate labels make every route identical
hard: A card labels 1564 as departure and 1565 as settlement. What conclusion fits?
The expedition began before establishing its Cebu base
The cards prove exact distances sailed
The expedition created Cebu's earlier history
Both labels describe one event on one day

label: Aims and roles
quiz: Which statement separates Legazpi's role from Urdaneta's contribution?

Legazpi sailed and navigated every ship alone

retry: What can a Spanish aim of occupation establish by itself?

That every island freely accepted the plan
That all outcomes were guaranteed
That no local society existed
hard: A report credits one leader with all expedition work. What revision is strongest?
Distinguish command, navigation and crew tasks without erasing local people
Keep the claim because leaders perform every task
Remove navigation and supplies from the explanation
Treat a sponsor's wish as proof of success

label: Local responses
quiz: Which statement reflects the evidence about local responses in Cebu?

All residents welcomed every demand without pressure

One agreement reveals every person's private thoughts

Why all residents must have shared one motive

Use the treaty as the exact thoughts of all people
Ignore all evidence of pressure or resistance
Assume nearby islands had no separate leaders

label: Cebu settlement
quiz: How should the 1565 Spanish settlement be described?

Only the size of the arriving ship

Effective authority over every other community
A continuing presence in Cebu

The existence of a recorded base

label: Return connection
quiz: Why was the return connection to Mexico important?

It made local responses unimportant

One person sailed the ship without a crew
A return route removed the need for supplies

hard: A report says a return route guaranteed the colony's success. What is missing?

Only the name of the returning ship
Proof that a route eliminates every danger
A claim that all people had the same interests
